subject: biochemistry
title: G-protein coupled receptors, second messengers, and receptor tyrosine kinase signaling

steps.tx: Transmembrane signaling translates extracellular endocrine cues into intracellular **responses**. G-protein coupled receptors contain seven membrane-spanning alpha helices coupled to heterotrimeric G-proteins (alpha, beta, gamma). Agonist binding induces GDP-GTP exchange on the G-alpha subunit, triggering dissociation from beta-gamma dimers. G-alpha-s activates adenylyl cyclase to generate cyclic AMP, which stimulates protein kinase A. G-alpha-i inhibits adenylyl cyclase, lowering cyclic AMP levels.
steps.say: GPCRs possess seven transmembrane helices coupled to heterotrimeric G-proteins. Agonist binding drives GTP loading onto G-alpha subunits. G-alpha-s activates adenylyl cyclase to generate cAMP and stimulate PKA, whereas G-alpha-i inhibits cAMP production.

steps.tx: The **phospholipase C** pathway mediates hormones signaling via G-alpha-q, such as angiotensin II, vasopressin (V1 receptor), and alpha-1 adrenergic agonists. Active G-alpha-q activates phospholipase C-beta, which hydrolyzes membrane phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate into inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG). Soluble IP3 diffuses to endoplasmic reticulum IP3-gated channels, releasing calcium into the cytosol. Elevated calcium and membrane DAG synergistically activate **protein kinase C**.
steps.say: The G-alpha-q pathway couples angiotensin II and alpha-1 receptors to phospholipase C, cleaving PIP2 into IP3 and DAG. IP3 triggers endoplasmic reticulum calcium release, while DAG and calcium activate protein kinase C.

steps.tx: Active G-alpha-q stimulates phospholipase C to cleave PIP2 into IP3 and diacylglycerol. Soluble IP3 releases intracellular calcium, which acts synergistically with DAG to activate protein kinase C. The phospholipase C pathway mediates hormones signaling via G-alpha-q, such as angiotensin II, vasopressin (V1 receptor), and alpha-1 adrenergic agonists.

steps.tx: Receptor **tyrosine kinases** mediate responses to growth factors like insulin, epidermal growth factor, and VEGF. Ligand binding triggers receptor dimerization and autophosphorylation of intracellular tyrosine residues. Phosphotyrosines recruit SH2-domain adaptors like Grb2 and SOS, which stimulate membrane-bound Ras to exchange GDP for GTP. Active Ras initiates the sequential Raf-MEK-ERK kinase cascade, driving nuclear transcription factors that promote cell cycle entry and proliferation.
steps.say: Receptor tyrosine kinases dimerize and autophosphorylate on tyrosine residues upon growth factor binding. Phosphotyrosines recruit Grb2-SOS to activate Ras-GTP, launching the Raf-MEK-ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase cascade to drive cell proliferation.

steps.tx: Mutations disrupting signaling cascades underlie human **endocrinopathies**. Albright hereditary osteodystrophy (pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A) results from inactivating mutations in the GNAS1 gene encoding G-alpha-s; target tissues fail to respond to parathyroid hormone, TSH, and gonadotropins despite elevated circulating hormone levels. Activating somatic GNAS1 mutations during embryogenesis cause McCune-Albright syndrome, characterized by polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, cafe-au-lait macules, and precocious puberty.
steps.say: Inactivating GNAS mutations encoding G-alpha-s cause pseudohypoparathyroidism with end-organ hormone resistance. Somatic activating GNAS mutations produce McCune-Albright syndrome with fibrous dysplasia, cafe-au-lait spots, and precocious puberty.
